flags: Allied Gold announced that first gold was poured at its Kurmuk Mine in Ethiopia, which it calls its newest producing mine.
With its Q3 2026 results, Allied Gold reported that ore had been introduced into the plant at Kurmuk and that the mine was in production, with a ramp-up expected through year-end.

Allied Gold stated that shareholder returns are expected to include a base dividend and a normal course issuer bid for up to 10% of the public float, subject to TSX approval and described as previously disclosed.

business_model.basis: Stated figures in the MD&A tables. The causal link is inferred.
business_model.claim: Realised gold price is the main revenue driver. Nine-month ounces sold fell to 286,380 from 304,722, yet nine-month revenue rose to $1,118,480 from $904,004 (revenue table in thousands).

business_model.basis: Mine-level costs are stated. The mix effect is inferred.

In 2025 revenue was 1,331,824 against 730,382, cost of sales excluding depreciation was 753,539, and gross profit was 506,542 (table in thousands). General and administrative expense was 120,794 (table in thousands). The main cost lines are mine operating costs, then administration.

quotes: Kurmuk is targeting production of 25,000 to 35,000 gold ounces in 2026, increasing sequentially month over month to 55,000 to 65,000 gold ounces in the first quarter of 2027, 240,000 to 270,000 gold ounces for full-year 2027 and approximately 300,000 gold ounces in 2028.
